info.title: Network Inventory
info.description:
Network Inventory API
Also referred to as NDS Inventory

Leverage the live network and traditional inventory systems to find the next available resource in real-time.
Eliminates conflicts between the network and inventory when selecting the next available resource.
Automation systems use this API to improve success rates.

post.description:
This API is deprecated. Please use /v1/domain/reservation instead.

The main concept to understand in this service is a domain. A domain is used to reserve a resource. sVlan is an example of a resource. The complete list of resources, their attributes, and descriptions are available in the schema. Their names end with Resource, SVlanResource...

Basics:

A domain is populated with information used to reserve a resource. It contains 3 main sections:

Information Section

These values are only used for logging and debugging. They have no impact on the actual service and are optional. They include: requestId, serviceId, circuitId

Allowable Section

These values are used to find the next available value of a resource. The required fields are: min, max. These values tell the service which range you want the next available value to be in.

Resource Section

These values specify the resource you want to reserve. They include the name of the resource, network information about the resource, and which inventory system you want to reserve the resource in.

Matching Resource Values:

If you want multiple resources to have the same value, you can put multiple resources in a domain. In the case of sVlan and subInterface, sometimes Engineering wants the values to match. This option provides that funcationality.

Request Details:

This serivce takes a domainRequest which contains a list of domains. In most cases there will only be 1 domain in the domainRequest. It allows multiple domains as a convience for calling systems. Submitting 2 domains in 1 domainRequest will accomplish the same as 2 domainRequests with 1 domain in each.

Service Details:

SOLR

In addition to the different inventory systems this service interacts with, there is also an internal SOLR index for each resource. This is used mostly for race conditions when multiple requests for the same resouce come into the service. The SOLR index is cleared out every 30 minutes. It is always used for each resource so it is not necessary to include in the request but can be if you like.

It also enables reservations of resources that do not live in any inventory system. Some resources, such as offnetSVlan, are not inventoried in any system. In these cases the network is the only source of record. All values in the network and SOLR are considered in use and will be excluded as possible next available values.

parameters.description: Defaults to false, set to true to run without updating inventory.

netexOracleSVlan.description: The first device is used to call the NetEx API, the 2nd is the device on our network.  This example treats the NetEx API similar to the network and will fail if there is an issue with the API.

layer3RouteTarget_layer3RouteDistinguish.description: The same pool of numbers is used to determine the layer3RouteTarget and layer3RouteDistinguisher so we only need to go SASI and VPN Inventory once under the layer3RouteTarget resource.

layer2VpnId.description: Since this is a global number and Sasi is the source, you probably do not want to continueOnFail.  Global numbers only need to be queried and updated once per Inventory System.

CommonDomainProps.description: These values are common for all domains.

requestId.description: Any unique value provided by the calling system.  There is no check to make sure this value is unique but if duplicates are used it makes debugging more difficult.  Only used for logging and debugging.

serviceId.description: Service id from order entry.  Only used for logging and debugging.

circuitId.description: Circuit id from order entry.  Only used for logging and debugging.

requestedValue.description: This value is used to reserve the resource.  It will only be used if it is available in the network/systems specified below.  If it is not available or not included in the request the next available value will be used to reserve the resource.

ignoreInventoryIfFull.description:
If no next available value is available, the range is full, ignore inventory and only try to find requestedValue/next available in the network !!!Think about the impact to inventory, this may be best suited for dynamic requests only?!!! Defaults to false if not included.
This is a self-closing tag. For JSON it needs to be an empty string.

skipInventoryIfAvailableInNetwork.description:
If there is a requestedValue and it is free in the network, skip querying/updating inventory. This is a legacy option. Shouldn't be used in almost all cases. Defaults to false if not included.
This is a self-closing tag. For JSON it needs to be an empty string.

numberOfValuesToTry.description: The default value for each resource is configured in nds.inventory.properties but this will override that value.  Most of the defaults are 5 but for busy specifc domains touching the same resource it could be helpful to have a larger value to avoid colisions and increase performance.

CommonDomainFilterProps.description: These values are common for all domains.

requestId.description: Any unique value provided by the calling system.  There is no check to make sure this value is unique but if duplicates are used it makes debugging more difficult.  Only used for logging and debugging.

AllowableObj.description: Used to calculate the next available value.

min.description: Minimum value to use for next available.

max.description: Maximum value to use for next available.

increment.description: Find the lowest used value then increment by this value to calculate the next available.

exclusion.description: Value(s) to exclude when calculating next available.

start.description: Start of range to exclude.  If end is not provided single value to exclude.

QueryObj.description:
Used to query a resource. This will get all in-use values.
If the property continueOnFail is excluded it defaults to false.

continueOnFail.description:
If there is any issue with the query it will be ignored.
For querying the network this should NOT be set in almost all cases. One of the main points of Network Inventory is to make sure we do not use in-use network values. For querying an inventory system this should be set in almost all cases. We do not want inventory to impact network builds.
This is a self-closing tag in XML. For JSON it needs to be an empty string.

VerifyObj.description:
Used to verify a resource. For resources that take too long to query this verify should be used. Instead of getting all in-use values like query, this will make 1 call with the possible next available value to see if it is available.
If the property continueOnFail is excluded it defaults to false.

continueOnFail.description:
If there is any issue with the verify it will be ignored.
For verifying the network this should NOT be set in almost all cases. One of the main points of Network Inventory is to make sure we do not use in-use network values. For verifying an inventory system this should be set in almost all cases. We do not want inventory to impact network builds.
This is a self-closing tag in XML. For JSON it needs to be an empty string.

UpdateObj.description:
Used to update a resource.
If the property continueOnFail is excluded it defaults to false.

continueOnFail.description:
If there is any issue with the update it will be ignored. This should be set in almost all cases. We do not want inventory to impact network builds.
This is a self-closing tag in XML. For JSON it needs to be an empty string.

NetworkQueryObj.description:
Used to query the network.
If the property query is excluded it defaults to query which is the most common case for interacting with the network.

NetworkVerifyObj.description: Used to verify with the network.

InventoryQueryUpdateObj.description:
Used to query and update an inventory system.
If both properties query and update are excluded it defaults to query and update, which is the most common case for interacting with an inventory system.

InventoryQueryObj.description:
Used to query an inventory system.
If query is excluded it defaults to query

InventoryVerifyObj.description: Used to verify with an inventory system.
